behaviors.description: A system-level design loads the whole System-Level required list. The case asserts: "All five System-Level required fragments load. Dropping adr-quality-readiness-checklist.md is the common miss, because the other four read as the obvious ones."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-design-system-level names all five System-Level required fragments and names neither maestro-flows.md nor contract-testing.md.

behaviors.description: An epic-level design loads the shorter Epic-Level list and leaves the conditional NFR fragment out. The case asserts: "Epic-level and system-level have different required lists, and the epic list is the shorter one. Loading the system-level set for an epic is over-loading, not thoroughness: the step says to load only what is relevant."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-design-epic-level names all four Epic-Level required fragments and names neither adr-quality-readiness-checklist.md nor maestro-flows.md.

behaviors.description: An epic-level design whose epic carries NFRs adds the conditional NFR fragment. The case asserts: "Tenant isolation is a security requirement and the 30s budget is a performance requirement, so the conditional NFR load fires. This case and the previous one differ only in whether the epic carries an NFR, which is what makes the pair worth running."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-design-epic-with-nfrs names all four Epic-Level required fragments plus nfr-criteria.md, and does not name maestro-flows.md.

behaviors.description: Pact relevance is decided by the artifacts in the repository. The case asserts: "The step says relevance is not a stack question: the consumer side of a contract is most often a frontend, and gating on backend/fullstack alone skips exactly the case Pact exists for. The .pacttest.ts files are the trigger, not the detected stack."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-design-pact-consumer-is-a-frontend names pactjs-utils-mandate.md alongside the three Epic-Level fragments, and names neither contract-testing.md nor maestro-flows.md.

behaviors.description: An epic-level design on a Gradle service loads the Epic-Level list and nothing Pact-related. The case asserts: "tea_use_pactjs_utils defaults to true and this repo has no Pact artifacts, no broker variables, and no microservice contract indicators the step names. The flag never means add contract tests to this project, so nothing Pact-related loads."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-design-backend-junit names all four Epic-Level required fragments and names none of pactjs-utils-mandate.md, contract-testing.md, maestro-flows.md, or playwright-utils-mandate.md.

stdin.value: The prompt the harness assembles for case test-design-system-level: the workflow's own step file or files, its resources/tea-index.csv, and that case's task, repository facts, and TEA config.
The prompt the harness assembles for case test-design-epic-level: the workflow's own step file or files, its resources/tea-index.csv, and that case's task, repository facts, and TEA config.

testData.setup: Every case runs against the checked-in bmad-testarch-test-design workflow: its step file or files named in requirementLinks, and its resources/tea-index.csv. The harness assembles one prompt per case from those files plus the case's task, repository facts, and TEA config, and writes it to the runner's standard input. The prompt bytes are evidence rather than declaration. This contract states what must be true of each case's selection, and the sealed run record carries the digest of the prompt that produced it, so a step-file edit that changes what the runner was asked shows up in the record instead of hiding inside a literal here.
testData.cleanup: Nothing is written. The runner reads a prompt from standard input and prints one JSON object to standard output; the workflow files and the eval data are read-only for the whole run.

safetyLimits: The runner receives a minimal environment: PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, the locale and proxy variables, and the selected vendor credential variables. Nothing else is passed through.
No credential value appears in a prompt, in a selection, or in a result file.
The runner writes nothing. The workflow step files, resources/tea-index.csv, and the eval data are read-only for the whole run.
requiredEvidence: The JSON object the runner printed on standard output for every case, in full.
The exit code of every case invocation.
The digest of the prompt each case was given, so a step-file edit that changed the question is visible in the record.
